messages.subject: Student--mentor contacts
parts:
I saw on the GSoC-Scilab project page that Scilab discourages contacts before the formal student application period. Instead students are asked to send questions to the corresponding Google group.

What is the reason for this? Or is it an official Google policy?

I can recognize a certain advantage in that mentors may prefer certain students (or have proposed the project to them) and may therefore not support other requests as extensively as to warrant a fair competition.

On the other hand, descriptions on the project page are in many cases not detailed enough to allow students a promising application.

How do other mentors here on GSoC-R handle this situation?

Best
Hans Werner

On Sun, 2012-03-18 at 04:07 -0700, HwB wrote:
> I saw on the GSoC-Scilab project page that Scilab discourages contacts
> before the formal student application period. Instead students are
> asked to send questions to the corresponding Google group.

The R Foundation suggestion is not so clear here:

http://rwiki.sciviews.org/doku.php?id=developers:projects:gsoc2012

we say "Students should look at the list of projects and see if any
project interests them. If so, email the project mentors to express your
interest, and describe any prior experience."
> What is the reason for this? Or is it an official Google policy?

This is not an official Google policy.

the official agenda item says: "Would-be student participants discuss
application ideas with mentoring organizations."

No method is proscribed for these discussions. If Scilab wants to do
that in the open on their Google group, that is certainly their
prerogative.

> I can recognize a certain advantage in that mentors may prefer certain
> students (or have proposed the project to them) and may therefore not
> support other requests as extensively as to warrant a fair
> competition.
>
> On the other hand, descriptions on the project page are in many cases
> not detailed enough to allow students a promising application.
>
> How do other mentors here on GSoC-R handle this situation?

I've been fielding email queries for a couple of months now on potential
projects. One of those queries was posted to this gsoc-r list, the
others I received via private email.

Regards,

- Brian
